examples.en: The police went out wearing body armor.
Reporters also wear body armor on battlefields.

examples.ko: 방탄복이 너무 무거워서 오래 입기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The vest is so heavy that it's hard to wear for long.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공이 방탄복 덕분에 살아났어요.
examples.en: The hero in the movie survived thanks to a bulletproof vest.

examples.ko: 새 방탄복을 사려면 돈이 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Buying a new bulletproof vest costs a lot.
When I took off the vest, sweat poured down.

explain: '방탄'은 총알을 막는다는 뜻이라 '방탄유리', '방탄조끼'에도 붙어요. 몸통만 덮는 조끼 모양은 '방탄조끼'라고도 많이 불러요.

phrases.en: A police officer in a bulletproof vest is standing there.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸통만 덮는 모양의 방탄복을 이렇게 많이 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: The common name for the vest-shaped type of body armor.

phrases.en: The windows of that car are bulletproof glass.
phrases.nuance_ko: '방탄'이 붙으면 총알을 막는 물건을 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 방탄 attached to a word means it stops bullets.

phrases.en: The work was over, so I took off the body armor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입는 것은 '입다', 벗는 것은 '벗다'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 입다 to put on and 벗다 to take off.

explain_en: '방탄' means stopping bullets, so it is also used in '방탄유리' (bulletproof glass) and '방탄조끼' (bulletproof vest). A vest that covers only the torso is often called '방탄조끼'.

examples.ko: 동생은 어릴 때부터 몸이 병약해서 자주 쉬었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling was sickly from childhood and rested often.

examples.ko: 병약한 아이를 키우는 부모님은 걱정이 많아요.
examples.en: Parents raising a sickly child worry a lot.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 병약한 역할을 아주 잘 연기해요.
examples.en: That actor plays frail, sickly characters very well.

examples.ko: 할머니는 젊을 때 병약하셨지만 지금은 건강하세요.
examples.en: Grandmother was sickly when she was young, but she is healthy now.
He looks sickly, but his stamina is good.
Working with such a frail body was really hard.

explain: 몸이 약하고 자주 아픈 사람을 말할 때 써요. 글이나 이야기에서 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '몸이 약해요'나 '골골해요'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 얼굴이 하얘서 좀 병약해 보여요.
phrases.en: That person has a pale face and looks a bit sickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습으로 몸이 약해 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone looks weak or sickly from their appearance.

phrases.en: My grandmother was sickly when she was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거의 모습을 말하는 해요체 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past tense in polite style, describing how someone used to be.

phrases.example: 저는 몸이 약해서 감기에 자주 걸려요.
phrases.en: I'm physically weak, so I catch colds often.
phrases.nuance_ko: '병약하다'와 같은 뜻의 쉬운 일상 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday expression with the same meaning as 병약하다.

explain_en: It describes someone who is physically weak and often ill. It appears often in writing and stories, while in daily talk people say '몸이 약해요' or '골골해요'.

examples.en: My fingers went stiff from the cold.
I sat too stiffly in the interview.

examples.ko: 아이가 사진을 찍을 때 뻣뻣이 서 있어요.
examples.en: The child stands stiffly when having a photo taken.

examples.ko: 풀을 먹인 셔츠가 뻣뻣이 서 있어요.
examples.en: The starched shirt stands up stiffly.
He walked past with his head held stiffly high.
I was so nervous on stage that my body froze up stiffly.

explain: 형용사 '뻣뻣하다'의 짝이에요. 몸이나 물건이 굳어서 잘 안 구부러질 때도 쓰고, 고개를 숙이지 않는 거만한 태도를 말할 때도 써요. 말할 때는 '뻣뻣하게'도 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 긴장해서 몸을 뻣뻣하게 하고 서 있었어요.
phrases.en: I was nervous and stood with my body stiff.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같고, 말할 때는 '뻣뻣이'보다 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning; more common in speech than 'ppeotppeosi'.

phrases.en: My neck is stiff after waking up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 '뻣뻣하다'의 활용으로, 몸이 굳은 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective 'ppeotppeothada' describing a stiff body part.

phrases.en: I was so scared that I just stood there stiffly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 움직이지 못하고 굳어서 서 있는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes standing frozen and unable to move.

explain_en: Body or attitude stiff and unbending, can sound negative. It is the adverb partner of the adjective '뻣뻣하다'. It describes a body or object that is stiff and does not bend, and also a proud attitude of not bowing one's head. In speech '뻣뻣하게' is also common.

t90.ax: I sat too stiffly in the interview.

examples.en: A baby's face has soft fuzz.

examples.ko: 복숭아 껍질에 솜털이 많이 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: There is a lot of fuzz on the peach skin.

examples.ko: 솜털 같은 구름이 하늘에 떠 있어요.
examples.en: Fluffy clouds are floating in the sky.
Because of the cold, the fine hair on my arm stood up.
Chicks are covered in yellow down.

examples.ko: 그는 아직 수염 대신 솜털만 나 있어요.
examples.en: He still has only peach fuzz instead of a beard.

explain: 아기, 병아리, 복숭아처럼 아주 가늘고 부드러운 털에 써요. 굵고 진한 '털'과 달리 연한 느낌이에요. 소름이 돋을 때 서는 것도 솜털이에요.

phrases.en: There is fine fuzz on the baby's arm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가는 털이 몸에 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when fine hair is present on the body.

phrases.en: I was scared and the hairs on my skin stood up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무섭거나 추워서 소름이 돋을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you get goosebumps from fear or cold.

phrases.en: This blanket is as soft as down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 부드러운 느낌을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to compare something to very soft touch.

explain_en: It is used for very thin, soft hair on babies, chicks, or peaches. Unlike thick, dark 털, it feels light and faint. The hair that stands up when you get goosebumps is also 솜털.

examples.en: My health condition is fine.
I got medicine from the school nurse.
The checkup result came out as good.
My stomach hurt, so I went to the school infirmary.
I was relieved to get a good rating.

examples.ko: 양호 등급이 나오면 다시 검사하지 않아도 돼요.
examples.en: If you get a good grade, you don't need to be tested again.

explain: '양호'는 소리가 같은 두 단어예요. 학교의 '양호실', '양호 선생님'은 학생의 건강을 돌본다는 뜻(養護)이고, 검사 결과의 '양호'는 상태가 좋다는 뜻(良好)이에요. 지금 학교의 공식 이름은 '보건실'이지만 말할 때는 아직 양호실이라고 많이 해요.

phrases.en: My head hurt, so I went to the school nurse's office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에서 아픈 학생을 돌보는 방이에요. 지금 공식 이름은 '보건실'이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The room where sick students are looked after; the official name today is 보건실.

phrases.en: My health checkup result came out as good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 검사나 점검 결과가 괜찮게 나왔을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the result of a test or inspection comes out fine.

phrases.en: This time my grades are fairly good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 좋지는 않지만 괜찮은 정도라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means not excellent but good enough.

explain_en: '양호' stands for two different words that sound the same. In '양호실' and '양호 선생님' it means looking after students' health (養護). On test or checkup results it means a good state (良好). The official school term is now '보건실', but people still often say '양호실'.

en: to be dizzy; to be faint

examples.en: I stood up suddenly and my head is spinning.

examples.ko: 높은 곳에서 아래를 보니 눈앞이 어찔했어요.
examples.en: When I looked down from a high place, everything swam before my eyes.
I felt dizzy, so I sat down for a moment.

examples.ko: 약 냄새를 맡자 어찔하면서 속이 울렁거렸어요.
examples.en: When I smelled the medicine, I felt dizzy and nauseous.
I walked across a dizzyingly high bridge.
I was so shocked that I felt faint for a moment.

explain: '어지럽다'가 계속 빙빙 도는 느낌이라면 '어찔하다'는 갑자기 순간적으로 핑 도는 느낌이에요. '아찔하다'와 비슷하게 쓰이는데 높은 곳이나 놀란 순간에 잘 어울려요. 보통 '머리가 어찔하다', '눈앞이 어찔하다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: I almost got hit by a car and felt dizzy with shock.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어찔하다'와 비슷하고 놀란 순간에 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 어찔하다 and used more often for startling moments.

phrases.en: My head suddenly started to spin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순간적으로 핑 도는 상태로 변하는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes suddenly becoming lightheaded.

phrases.en: I feel dizzy when I stand up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 느낌을 명사 앞에서 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun to describe the sensation.

explain_en: While '어지럽다' feels like a continuous spinning, '어찔하다' is a sudden, momentary swoon. It is used similarly to '아찔하다' and fits high places or startling moments. It is usually said as '머리가 어찔하다' or '눈앞이 어찔하다'.

examples.ko: 오늘 우리 팀 선발 투수는 우완이에요.
examples.en: Our team's starting pitcher today is a right-hander.

examples.ko: 새로 온 우완 투수가 공이 정말 빨라요.
examples.en: The new right-handed pitcher throws really fast.
It is a team with more right-handers than left-handers.
That player is called the right-handed ace.

examples.ko: 그 투수는 우완이지만 왼손으로도 글씨를 써요.
examples.en: That pitcher is right-handed but also writes with his left hand.

examples.ko: 마지막 이닝에 우완 불펜이 마운드에 올라왔어요.
examples.en: A right-handed reliever came up to the mound in the last inning.

explain: 주로 야구에서 '우완 투수'처럼 오른팔로 던지는 투수를 말할 때 써요. 반대말은 '좌완'이에요. 일상에서 오른팔을 말할 때는 '오른팔'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 팀에는 빠른 공을 던지는 우완 투수가 있어요.
phrases.en: That team has a right-handed pitcher who throws fast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야구에서 오른팔로 던지는 투수를 말하는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for a right-arm pitcher in baseball.

phrases.example: 우리 팀 우완 에이스가 오늘 나와요.
phrases.en: Our team's right-handed ace pitches today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팀에서 가장 믿는 오른팔 투수를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to the team's most trusted right-handed pitcher.

phrases.en: I hurt my right arm while throwing a ball.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야구 밖의 일상에서는 '우완' 대신 '오른팔'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Outside baseball, people say 오른팔 instead of 우완.

explain_en: It is used mainly in baseball, as in '우완 투수' for a pitcher who throws with the right arm. The opposite is '좌완'. In daily life, the right arm is just '오른팔'.

examples.ko: 약이 캡슐로 되어 있어서 삼키기 쉬워요.
examples.en: The medicine is in capsules, so it's easy to swallow.

examples.ko: 저는 아침마다 비타민 캡슐을 하나씩 먹어요.
examples.en: Every morning I take one vitamin capsule.

examples.ko: 커피 머신에 캡슐을 넣고 버튼을 눌렀어요.
examples.en: I put a capsule in the coffee machine and pressed the button.
Please take this capsule with water.
The space capsule landed safely in the sea.

examples.ko: 어렸을 때 친구들과 타임 캡슐을 땅에 묻었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, my friends and I buried a time capsule in the ground.

explain: 알약 모양의 약이나 커피 캡슐처럼 작은 통 모양에 써요. 약은 '알약', '가루약'과 구분해서 말해요. '타임캡슐', '우주 캡슐'처럼 다른 말과 붙여 쓰는 일도 많아요.

phrases.en: I make coffee with a coffee capsule every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계에 넣어 쓰는 작은 통 모양의 커피를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to small pods you put into a coffee machine.

phrases.en: At graduation, my friends and I buried a time capsule.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미래에 열어 볼 물건을 넣는 통을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A container filled with items to be opened in the future.

phrases.en: Take one capsule after a meal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약을 먹는 양을 말할 때 숫자와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with a number to say how much medicine to take.

explain_en: It is used for small shell-shaped things such as medicine capsules and coffee capsules. For medicine, Koreans distinguish it from 알약 (tablets) and 가루약 (powder). It also appears in compounds like 타임캡슐 and 우주 캡슐.

examples.en: After a baby is born, the umbilical cord is cut.
The mother and baby are connected by the umbilical cord.
The father cut the umbilical cord himself.
The place where the umbilical cord falls off becomes the belly button.
The cord was wrapped around the neck, so we were worried.
The umbilical cord delivers nutrition to the baby.

explain: 엄마 배 속에서 아기가 영양을 받는 줄이에요. 태어난 뒤에 자르고 남은 자리가 '배꼽'이에요. 의학에서는 '제대'라고도 하지만 일상에서는 '탯줄'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The father cut the umbilical cord himself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기가 태어난 뒤에 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation after a baby is born.

phrases.en: A baby receives nutrition through the umbilical cord.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탯줄이 하는 일을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain what the cord does.

phrases.en: The place where the cord falls off becomes the belly button.
phrases.nuance_ko: 태어난 뒤 탯줄이 저절로 떨어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the cord comes off by itself after birth.

explain_en: It is the cord through which a baby receives nourishment in the womb. After birth it is cut, and the place left behind is the '배꼽' (belly button). Medicine also uses '제대', but daily speech says '탯줄'.

examples.ko: 이 상자는 모서리가 각져서 손이 아파요.
examples.en: This box has sharp corners and hurts my hand.
He has a face with a square jaw.
Angular stones are dangerous to throw.
I made it round, but one side came out angular.
A cup without sharp edges is comfortable in the hand.
I folded the paper at sharp angles and made a box.

explain: '각지다'는 둥글지 않고 모서리가 반듯하거나 뾰족한 모양이에요. '각진 얼굴, 턱, 어깨'처럼 사람의 모습에 많이 쓰고, 반대는 '둥글다'예요. '각진 어깨'는 어깨선이 곧고 넓어 보이는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The angular-shaped plate is pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 '각진'으로 활용해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the form 각진 to describe a noun after it.

phrases.en: This bag has angular corners.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장 끝에서 쓰는 해요체 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form used at the end of a sentence.

phrases.example: 이 의자는 모서리가 각지지 않아서 안전해요.
phrases.en: This chair's corners aren't sharp, so it's safe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 둥글고 부드러운 모양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a round, soft shape.

explain_en: '각지다' describes a shape with straight or sharp corners rather than a round one. It is common for people's looks, as in '각진 얼굴', '각진 턱' and '각진 어깨'. Its opposite is '둥글다'. A '각진 어깨' means a straight, broad shoulder line.

examples.en: I got rained on and look like a total wreck.
After working all night, I came home looking a mess.
Where are you going looking like that?

examples.ko: 머리도 안 빗고 거지꼴 그대로 나왔어요.
examples.en: He came out looking a mess, without even combing his hair.
After the hike, everyone looked like a mess.
Even though he looked shabby, his expression was bright.

explain: 옷이나 모습이 너무 지저분하고 초라할 때 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. 보통 '거지꼴이 되다', '거지꼴로 다니다'처럼 써요. 남에게 직접 말하면 무례하니 자기 모습이나 친한 사이에서만 쓰세요.

phrases.en: I worked all night, so I look a total mess.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거지꼴'보다 덜 거칠게, 모습이 아주 엉망일 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A milder way than '거지꼴' to say someone looks like a complete mess.

phrases.en: It's fine to walk around looking shabby at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거지꼴'을 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이고, 자기 모습이나 친한 사이에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation with '거지꼴'; use it about yourself or with close friends.

phrases.example: 시험 때문에 며칠째 거지꼴을 하고 있어요.
phrases.en: I've been looking miserable for days because of exams.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거지꼴이 되다'는 변화를, '거지꼴을 하다'는 그런 모습을 하고 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '거지꼴이 되다' describes becoming shabby; '거지꼴을 하다' describes being in that state.

explain_en: It is a casual word for looking very untidy and shabby, typically in '거지꼴이 되다' or '거지꼴로 다니다'. It is rude to say directly to someone, so use it about yourself or with close friends.

en: to be beautiful; to be pretty; to be lovely

examples.en: The bride in a hanbok is really lovely.
The child's hands are so delicate that I hesitate even to touch them.

examples.ko: 곱디고운 목소리로 할머니가 노래를 불러 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother sang for us in a sweet, lovely voice.
The autumn maple leaves have turned a beautiful color.

examples.ko: 세월이 흘러 곱디곱던 얼굴에도 주름이 생겼어요.
examples.en: As time passed, wrinkles appeared even on her once lovely face.

examples.ko: 곱디고울 때 사진을 많이 찍어 두세요.
examples.en: Take lots of photos while she is at her prettiest.

explain: '곱다'를 강하게 말한 표현으로, '높디높다', '크디크다'처럼 형용사를 반복해서 강조하는 꼴이에요. 얼굴, 색, 마음씨, 손에 쓰고 글이나 노랫말에서 자주 보여요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '곱디고와요', '곱디고운'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: My grandmother has a lovely, kind heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습뿐 아니라 마음씨에도 쓸 수 있고 글에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: It can describe a kind heart as well as looks, and often appears in writing.

phrases.en: The color of the hanbok is so beautiful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 말할 때 'ㅂ'이 '와'로 바뀌어 '곱디고와요'가 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: In polite speech the ㅂ changes, giving 곱디고와요.

phrases.en: The baby's face is so lovely.
phrases.nuance_ko: '곱디곱다'의 기본형으로, 강조하지 않고 평범하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic form of 곱디곱다, used without emphasis.

explain_en: Intensified soft, delicate beauty, such as clothes or a gentle face. It is an intensified form of '곱다', repeating the adjective just like '높디높다' and '크디크다'. It is used for faces, colors, hearts and hands, and often seen in writing and lyrics. It is a 'ㅂ' irregular adjective: '곱디고와요', '곱디고운'.

t90.ax: The bride in a hanbok is really lovely.

en: to be thick; to be deep

examples.en: That actor has a deep, thick voice, which is impressive.
The wooden pillar looks thick and sturdy.
Big, thick raindrops started to fall.
Please write the letters in bold, thick strokes.
These potatoes are really big and thick.

examples.ko: 그 형은 어릴 때부터 팔뚝이 굵직했어요.
examples.en: That older guy has had thick forearms since he was little.

explain: '굵다'보다 꽤 굵고 듬직한 느낌이에요. 목소리나 선, 나무에 쓰고, '굵직한 사건'처럼 크고 중요한 일을 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I wrote my name in thick letters.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글씨나 선이 굵고 눈에 잘 띌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for thick, easy-to-see lettering or lines.

phrases.en: There were many major events this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크고 중요한 일을 말하는 비유적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for big, important events.

phrases.en: I drew a thick line with a pen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사로 쓰면 어떻게 그리거나 쓰는지 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: As an adverb it tells how something is drawn or written.

explain_en: Sturdy thick build or deep, full voice; sounds reassuring (굵직한 목소리) Compared with '굵다', it feels solidly thick and dependable. It's used for voices, lines and trees, and also for big, important matters, as in '굵직한 사건'.

t90.ax: Big, thick raindrops started to fall.

examples.ko: 우리 아기는 낯가림이 심해서 처음 보는 사람 품에 안 가요.
examples.en: My baby is shy with strangers and won't go into a new person's arms.

examples.ko: 저는 낯가림이 있어서 새 모임이 어색해요.
examples.en: I'm shy around new people, so new gatherings feel awkward.

examples.ko: 낯가림 때문에 처음에는 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: Because I'm shy with strangers, I couldn't even speak at first.

examples.ko: 동생은 낯가림이 없어서 누구하고나 잘 놀아요.
examples.en: My younger sibling isn't shy and plays well with anyone.
As my shyness with strangers lessened, I made more friends.
They say a child's stranger shyness is part of growing up.

explain: 동사 '낯을 가리다'의 명사형으로 '낯가림이 심하다/없다'처럼 써요. 아기의 낯가림과 어른의 성격을 말할 때 둘 다 써요.

phrases.en: My daughter is very shy with strangers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정도가 크다고 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for a strong degree.

phrases.en: The baby is shy of strangers, so it cries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '낯가림'의 원래 동사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The original verb phrase behind the noun '낯가림'.

phrases.example: 그 아이는 낯가림이 없어서 누구와도 잘 놀아요.
phrases.en: That child isn't shy with strangers, so he plays well with anyone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대로 사람을 쉽게 만나는 성격을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite: describes someone who meets people easily.

explain_en: It is the noun form of the verb '낯을 가리다' and is used as '낯가림이 심하다/없다'. It describes both a baby's stranger anxiety and an adult's personality.

examples.en: This product only comes in a single color.

examples.ko: 모든 학생을 단일한 기준으로 평가하기는 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to judge every student by a single standard.
The menu is just one item, so choosing is easy.
This shop sells only a single menu item.
The once-unified market split into several.
The company manages all its branches in a unified way.

explain: '하나'만 있다는 뜻인데 일상에서는 '한 가지'나 '하나뿐인'이라고 말해요. '단일'은 '단일 메뉴', '단일 팀'처럼 명사 앞에 붙는 쓰임이 많아요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '다양하다'예요.

phrases.en: This restaurant sells only a single menu item.
phrases.nuance_ko: '단일'을 명사 앞에 붙여 '하나뿐인'이라는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: '단일' placed before a noun means 'only one'.

phrases.en: This problem has only one answer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '단일하다' 대신 이렇게 말하는 경우가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech, people often say this instead of '단일하다'.

phrases.example: 우리 반 학생들의 생각은 단일하지 않아요.
phrases.en: The students in our class don't all think the same way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어의 부정형으로, 여러 가지가 섞여 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning there is a mix of several kinds.

explain_en: It means there is only one, but in daily speech people say 한 가지 or 하나뿐인. 단일 often attaches before a noun, as in '단일 메뉴' or '단일 팀'. The opposite idea is 다양하다.
